## Choose the index law {#choose-law}

For like bases, add the indices when multiplying and subtract them when dividing. Use a common denominator for the arithmetic.

:::::: {.example-pair}

::::: {.model}

<h3>Worked example</h3>

$x^{\frac34}\times x^{\frac12}$

::: {.fragment}

[Multiply like bases. Add their indices.]{.annotation}

$=x^{\frac34+\frac12}$

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Write both indices in quarters.]{.annotation}

$=x^{\frac34+\frac24}=x^{\frac54}$

:::

:::::

::::: {.paper}

::: {.fragment}

<h3>Your turn</h3>

$x^{\frac34}\div x^{\frac12}$

The operation changes to division. Choose the law, then simplify on paper.

:::

::: {.fragment}

[Check your working]{.annotation}

$=x^{\frac34-\frac12}$

$=x^{\frac34-\frac24}=x^{\frac14}$

:::
